extracted.intended_audience: DHS management (ICOFR PMO), component CFOs, internal auditors, OIG and federal auditors
extracted.subtask_description: Audit/reporting guidance and evaluation criteria for a federal agency's implementation of OMB Circular No. A-123 (Appendix A) and internal control over financial reporting (ICOFR), as applied to DHS FY2008. Focuses on planning, testing, monitoring, documentation, and assurance reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency responsibilities under OMB Circular No. A-123
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies and individual Federal managers must take systematic and proactive measures to (i) develop and implement appropriate, cost-effective internal control for results-oriented management; (ii) assess the adequacy of internal control in Federal programs and operations; (iii) separately assess and document internal control over financial reporting consistent with the process defined in Appendix A; (iv) identify needed improvements; (v) take corresponding corrective action; and (vi) report annually on internal control through management assurance statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core set of managerial obligations driving ICOFR activities, including development, assessment, remediation, and annual reporting (Secretary's/agency head Assurance Statement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendix A ICOFR assessment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Management must separately assess and document internal control over financial reporting consistent with the process defined in Appendix A of OMB Circular No. A-123.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix A governs scope determination, selection of key processes/controls, documentation, testing approach (TOD/TOE), materiality, and the form/content of the management assurance. The audit used Appendix A as the criteria for assessing DHS' workpapers and process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish organizational structure for implementation and oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm whether management established an organizational structure to effectively implement, direct, and oversee the assessment process. The Circular suggests a Senior Management Council and a Senior Assessment Team or equivalent structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An explicit governance structure (roles, responsibilities, councils/teams) is expected to guide planning, testing, remediation, monitoring, and compilation of the Assurance Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope determination and identification of significant processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish an approach to determine the scope of the assessment. The scope of the assessment includes identifying significant financial reports and key processes/controls/transactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope should be based on materiality calculations and risk-based prioritization; scope decisions (why processes/components were selected or excluded) must be documented and justified, including treatment of new/merged components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk-based approach to testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm whether management used a risk-based approach to testing and whether the test plan reflects an efficient approach to testing based on materiality and risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing strategy should prioritize processes with highest risk and materiality, but may consider qualitative factors (e.g., news/media coverage); the linkage between risk assessments (quantitative and qualitative) and the resulting test plan should be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform both Tests of Design (TOD) and Tests of Operating Effectiveness (TOE) for material processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform both tests of design and tests of operating effectiveness for all material processes across the Department to identify any potential material weaknesses or significant deficiencies not identified through tests of design or in the external audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relying only on TODs (design tests) without TOEs can fail to identify operating deficiencies. If a TOE is performed, TOD should be reassessed/re-performed or documentation must show TOD was reassessed for current year and any changes noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate and document IT general controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm whether management evaluated and documented IT general controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ITGC evaluation is required where IT affects financial reporting; documentation should evidence the evaluation and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate and document compliance with key laws and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm whether management evaluated and documented compliance with key laws and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the 'LR' (laws and regulations) assertion is tested, cite each specific law or regulation; aggregate results over direct and material laws/regulations for each Internal Control Component to determine overall compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document planning decisions, linkages, and qualitative factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly document the linkage and/or process of the qualitative and quantitative factors considered during planning to the resulting test plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If qualitative considerations (e.g., media attention, organizational change) influence selection of processes to test, those considerations and how they affected the test plan must be recorded to allow third-party review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document monitoring activities and results
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement an overall system of documenting the Department's monitoring activities and results to allow third party review of such materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitoring documentation should include the nature, timing, extent, and results of monitoring work (not just that monitoring occurred), so monitoring can be evaluated for sufficiency and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust monitoring procedures to detect new deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform more thorough monitoring procedures to identify changes to controls, control risks, or the operation of controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: implement a more rigorous review to ensure proper accounting rules are applied; monitor high-risk areas such as segregation of duties more closely; perform detailed walkthroughs and interviews throughout the year; expand monitoring activities year-round; perform some monitoring at detailed/lower management levels while involving senior management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and sufficiency of key controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Reassess the controls identified and determine if additional key controls should be tested to cover all risks and/or assertions related to significant line items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management must identify enough key controls to detect weaknesses affecting significant financial-statement line items; failure to identify sufficient key controls can lead to undiscovered significant deficiencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of results over laws and internal control components
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate the results of testing over direct and material laws and regulations for each Internal Control Component so that Management can determine its overall compliance with the law or regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregation assists in forming component-level and department-level conclusions about compliance and control effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and assessment of compensating controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifically identify each compensating control as well as assess its design, implementation, and operating effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a compensating control is asserted, it must be referenced in the Summary of Aggregated Deficiencies and evaluated for effectiveness; if no compensating control exists, document that consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: TOE documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each Tests of Operating Effectiveness (TOE) tested, document: (a) Methodology used to select the sample (i.e., computer sampling tool); (b) A description of the population sampled; (c) Procedures, if any, to determine the completeness of the population from which samples were selected; and (d) Justification of the sample size rationale based on appropriate guidance and the type of control tested (i.e., yearly, monthly, recurring, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TOE workpapers should enable a third party to understand sampling approach, population completeness, sample size rationale (with reference to GAO/PCIE Financial Audit Manual or Playbook), and to reproduce or evaluate conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistently identify period of control testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistently identify the period for which controls are tested (i.e., as of September 30, 2008).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test documentation should state explicitly the period covered so reviewers can determine whether coverage aligns with reporting dates and assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance statement must reflect amount of work and scope limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm whether submission of the assurance statement by the agency head accurately reflects the amount of work completed (e.g., agencies implementing a multi-year plan will need to identify a scope limitation) and the results of the assessments performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assurance statements should disclose scope limitations and be consistent with testing coverage; they should not overstate assurance if testing was limited or multi-year plans delay full coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-year implementation plan content and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm whether management submitted a multi-year implementation plan that: (i) states why the agency requires more than one year to execute its plan; (ii) provides for identifying, testing, and assessing a significant percentage of its key business processes and controls in each year; (iii) demonstrates how the agency will meet the OMB Circular No. A-123, Appendix A requirements; and (iv) is reviewed and accepted by OMB.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For agencies using multi-year approaches (allowed with OMB approval), the plan must be explicit about schedule, annual coverage expectations, and must be implemented in substantial accordance with the approved plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of other audits and information to support conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm whether management used the results of its testing, and considered information gathered during the financial statement audit and other audits or reviews, to support its conclusion whether internal controls over financial reporting were properly designed and operating effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management should integrate external auditor findings, GAO/OIG results, and other relevant reviews into its assessment and documentation to avoid gaps and to corroborate conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and severity thresholds for control deficiencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal control deficiency: design or operation of a control does not allow management or employees to prevent or detect misstatements on a timely basis. Significant deficiency: a control deficiency, or combination of control deficiencies, that adversely affects the ability to initiate, authorize, record, process, or report financial data reliably such that there is more than a remote likelihood that a misstatement that is more than inconsequential will not be prevented or detected. Material weakness: a significant deficiency, or combination of significant deficiencies, that results in more than a remote likelihood that a material misstatement will not be prevented or detected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions set the thresholds for classifying findings and drive remediation/prioritization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include new or recently merged/consolidated components in ICOFR scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the new or recently merged/consolidated components in the scope of the ICOFR planning to identify any potential material weaknesses or significant deficiencies not identified in the external audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New or reorganized components should not be excluded from assessment simply due to standing-up operations; exclusion must be justified and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform testing of specific material processes (e.g., Financial Systems Security, Budgetary Resources Management)
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement testing of ICOFR over material processes (for example, Financial Systems Security and Budgetary Resources Management at TSA) to identify any potential material weaknesses or significant deficiencies not identified in the external audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing should cover material and significant processes across components rather than focusing only on remediation where controls are known to be ineffective.
